name: dev.turva/turva-mcp
description: Read-only MCP server for turva.dev with the service catalog, prices and published scan evidence.

tools.name: get_services
tools.description: Returns turva.dev's service catalog with prices, the working terms of an engagement, the contract terms of the legal page and an outline of the published sample audit report. Use this when a user asks what turva.dev offers or costs, what access an engagement needs, what the contract says or what a delivered report contains. Start here too when a user asks in general what turva.dev does. For the principles behind every engagement use get_principles, and for who runs turva.dev, how to reach it and how personal data is handled use get_contact. It makes no network request: the data is compiled into the server, is the same on every call and changes only on deploy. The contract terms are quoted in full, not summarized.

tools.name: get_agent_readiness
tools.description: Returns turva.dev's own agent-readiness reading from the independent scanner isitagentready.com, with the overall score and level, the category sub-scores and the measurement date. Use this when a user asks for turva.dev's agent-readiness score or level, or wants to check the claim behind the audit service. For web and email security scan results use get_security_evidence, and when a user asks for evidence in general, call both. The reading is compiled into the server and changes only on deploy, so check its date. The scanner link in the result opens the scanner's start page, where anyone can run a new check, and not the recorded reading.

tools.name: get_security_evidence
tools.description: Returns the security scan results for turva.dev's own domain from Hardenize and two Internet.nl tests, one for the website and one for its mail, covering HTTPS, DNSSEC, RPKI, IPv6 and email authentication. Use this when a user asks how turva.dev's own domain is secured or configured. For the agent-readiness score use get_agent_readiness, and when a user asks for evidence in general, call both. It makes no network request and runs no scan: the results are compiled into the server, are the same on every call and change only on deploy. Each scan carries its own date and a link to the provider's public report, so check the date before you quote a result.

tools.name: get_principles
tools.description: Returns the four principles turva.dev applies to every engagement, each with its reason: async-only, least access, each fix checked with a scanner or a direct test, and open and verifiable. Use this when a user asks what turva.dev stands by or why it works the way it does, for example why an engagement runs in writing, with no calls and no calendar links. For an engagement's terms and prices use get_services, and to start one use get_contact. It makes no network request: the principles are compiled into the server, are the same on every call and change only on deploy. They state the policy for every engagement, not the terms of a particular one.

tools.name: get_contact
tools.description: Returns who runs turva.dev, how to reach it and how it handles personal data: the operator's legal and business details, the contact channels with their reply times, the first steps to start an engagement, and the privacy sections of the legal page quoted in full. Use this when a user asks who is behind turva.dev, for its legal details, how to contact it or start an audit, or how personal data is handled. For the services, prices, the access an engagement needs and the contract terms use get_services. It makes no network request and sends no message for the user: the data is compiled into the server, is the same on every call and changes only on deploy. Engagements run in writing, so the result offers no call or meeting booking.

tools.name: get_page_index
tools.description: Lists the pages of turva.dev, read from the site's /llms.txt when you call it: the main pages, the sample report, the guides and the blog posts, grouped under the index's sections, each with a title and a path that get_page accepts as it stands. Use this when you do not know which pages exist or which path a page has, then call get_page with the path. For the services and prices use get_services, and for who runs turva.dev use get_contact. Each call sends one GET request to turva.dev through a service binding that reaches no other host and forwards nothing from your request. It lists only turva.dev's own pages, each once, and it does not follow a redirect. A tool error comes back when the site answers with a status other than 2xx or with more than 262144 bytes, or when the index lists no pages.

tools.name: get_page
tools.description: Returns the markdown of one page on turva.dev, read from the site when you call it. The markdown is the main content the site serves to a request for text/markdown, without the frame around it, so it is not the HTML page byte for byte. Use this when a user asks about a guide, a blog post or a page the other tools do not cover, or wants a page's own wording. If you do not know the path, call get_page_index first. For the services and prices use get_services, and for who runs turva.dev use get_contact. Each call sends one GET request to turva.dev through a service binding that reaches no other host and forwards nothing from your request. It refuses a path outside turva.dev, an answer longer than 262144 bytes and any status other than 2xx. It does not follow a redirect: when the new path is on turva.dev, the error names it and you call again with it.

path.description: A path on turva.dev that starts with a single slash, has no query string and is in normal form, for example /guides/llms-txt or /agent-readiness-audit. Call get_page_index to list the paths.
